learning.title: How studying works
learning.subtitle: Seven steps from your request to your diploma. Study from any country and keep your job.
learning.photoAlt: Hands typing on a laptop with code and design layouts on screen, a notebook beside it

steps.title: Request
steps.text: A manager helps you choose a profession and opens free access to the introductory lessons for 7 days.

steps.title: Contract and payment
steps.text: Pay in full with 10% off or in 0% installments. Platform access opens 15 minutes after payment.

steps.title: Cohort start
steps.text: You get the first module, join the group chat in Telegram and meet your mentor.

steps.title: A study week
steps.text: 2–3 recorded lessons, two 1.5-hour webinars and a practical assignment. 8–10 hours a week.

steps.title: Projects
steps.text: Every module ends with a practical project. By the end you have 4 to 6 portfolio pieces.

steps.title: Final project
steps.text: On most courses it is for a real client, and you defend it in front of the teacher.

steps.title: Certificate and job
steps.text: An electronic certificate with a verification number and six months of career center support.

learning.pause: Need a break? Move to the next cohort free of charge — once per course, for up to 3 months.

teachers.title: Teachers
teachers.subtitle: Every course is led by a practitioner from a product company. Mentors review assignments — no more than 25 students each.

career.title: Certificate and job support
career.text: Help with finding a job is included in every course. The career center works with you during the course and for 6 months after graduation.
career.photoAlt: A graduate shaking hands with an interviewer
points: A portfolio on GitHub, Behance or as case studies
Referrals to partner companies and internships for top students
career.certificate: A certificate with a unique number is issued after you defend your final project and complete 80% of assignments. An English version is free on request.
career.note: We do not guarantee employment — the result depends on you too. On average, graduates find their first job in 3 months.

items.name: Olga Mironova
items.text: I came from accounting and was afraid I couldn't do it without drawing skills. It turned out interface design is about logic and research. The final project for a real client became the main case in my portfolio.

items.name: Artem Zakharov
items.text: The most valuable part was code review. My mentor went through every assignment and explained why not to write it that way. At interviews I was asked things we had already covered in mock interviews.

items.name: Ekaterina Volkova
items.text: I was a marketer living in Excel. Now I write SQL queries and build dashboards. Statistics was explained from scratch, without scary maths.

items.name: Igor Savchenko
items.text: I studied in the evenings after work: 7 pm webinars were convenient and recordings saved me in busy weeks. I took a break because of a move and was transferred to the next cohort, no questions asked.

items.name: Natalia Kim
items.text: I launched my first ad campaign with a real budget in the second month. Now I run promotion for two online stores.

items.name: Maxim Belousov
items.text: The career center helped me rewrite my CV and sent it to partner companies. I did an internship at one of them and stayed on staff.

payment.title: Payment
payment.subtitle: The price covers everything: lessons, webinars, assignment reviews, projects, job support and the certificate. No extra fees.

options.title: Interest-free installments
options.text: Up to 12 months through partner banks, first payment a month later. Non-Russian citizens can pay the school in two or three parts.

options.title: Discounts
options.text: 10% off when you pay for the whole course at once, 15% off a second course for students and graduates. Discounts don't combine.

options.title: Refunds
options.text: 100% in the first 14 days with no questions asked; later, for the modules you haven't started. Money arrives within 10 working days.

options.title: Payment methods
options.text: Visa, Mastercard and MIR cards, SBP, or an invoice for companies paying for their employees.
